"Below are questions proposed for a research problem, each with the reframing behind it. Classify each one.
kind: \"reframe\" if it changes what is computed, measured or ordered so that more compute buys something it did not before; \"copies\" if it only runs the same computation more times, on more items, or side by side; \"other\" otherwise.
meets_criterion: \"yes\" or \"no\" for this criterion: none given; answer NA
Give for each a quote from the proposal and a reason of at most 25 words. Decide only from the text below; do not use tools.
Problem:
**ml-ensemble-extremes · Ensemble size for rare extremes in a machine-learned weather ensemble.** seed pick · compute tested: yes · plan expects: the lever · PASS

**Question.** Does 10 to 1,000 AIFS-ENS members beat 50 for top-percentile wind, temperature, and rain probability forecasts, or does shared model error cap the skill?

**What is known.** HENS Part 2: 7,424 SFNO members per day for 92 summer-2023 dates; showed huge ensembles sample 4-sigma tails and reduce outliers. Whether AIFS-ENS, whose members are exchangeable draws of one afCRPS-trained distribution, keeps gaining skill past 50 members or saturates from shared model error.

**Hypothesis.** More members keep helping: 1,000 members sample top-percentile tails far better than 50, so extreme-event scores keep improving [s_hens].

**If compute is the lever.** Skill on top-percentile wind, temperature, and rain keeps rising past 50 members: 1,000 members sharpen the tails and improve extreme-event scores.

**If not.** Skill flattens near 50 members: members are exchangeable draws of one trained distribution, so shared model error caps tail sharpness and extra members add nothing.

**Test.** Run 7,000 fifteen-day AIFS-ENS v1 forecasts (7 dates x 1,000 members) on eight A100 40 GB GPUs; subsample 10-1,000 members, score top-percentile wind/temperature/rain probabilities against ERA5 with fair CRPS and Brier scores, and test whether skill still rises past 50 members.

*Compute axis.* Ensemble members per forecast: 10–1,000 members, 6 levels. Closest prior: 7,424 [s_hens], not beyond it.

*Restructuring.* none.

**Check first.** Reproduce the published 4-minute N320 member time and 38 GB memory; one control run must match ECMWF open data within ensemble spread [s_crps_paper]. Tolerance: timing within +/-25% of 4 min; 38 GB memory fits; control field within the ensemble's own member-to-member spread at each lead time (GPUs are non-deterministic, so exact reproduction is not expected).

**Would not show.** Applies to AIFS-ENS v1 medium-range extremes on 7 dates; not a multi-season reforecast, other models, subseasonal leads, or direct proof that shared error causes any saturation.

*Cost.* Plans $963.17 of the $1,000 budget over 74.3 machine-hours, leaving $36.83. Main guess: peak filesystem usage [g], measured after $19.90 of spend; the budget is reached if it is 15× higher. Full scale: A 30-date multi-season reforecast at 1,000 members, $3,980, 3.98× the budget.
Proposals: [{\"index\":1,\"bottleneck\":\"Members are exchangeable draws of one afCRPS-trained distribution, so any score converges at Monte Carlo rate to that distribution's intrinsic skill; past a few hundred members the 6-level ladder mostly buys a tighter estimate of a number already reached, and 7 dates leave between-date variance untouched no matter how many members are added.\",\"assumption\":\"The decision-relevant quantity is skill at particular member counts (10-1,000), so it must be measured by running and scoring every level of the ladder.\",\"reframe\":\"Change what is measured: instead of skill-at-N, estimate the infinite-member skill S_inf and the convergence exponent per case by extrapolation across nested subsamples, plus a date-bootstrap confidence interval on the 50-to-1,000 gain. The deliverable becomes 'headroom to the shared-error cap' and 'is the gain even resolvable on 7 dates', which settles the root question with a fraction of the planned spend.\",\"question\":\"For top-percentile 10 m wind at leads of 5-10 days, is the 500-to-1,000-member change in fair CRPS consistent with a fitted O(1/N) Monte Carlo decay, and does the across-date bootstrap CI of the 50-to-1,000 gain exclude zero?\",\"measure\":\"Subsample the saved member fields from the cheap pilot stage (or the planned runs) at 50/100/200/400/800 members, score each nested subset, fit score(N) = S_inf - a*N^(-alpha) per date-variable-lead, and bootstrap the 7 dates for the 50-vs-1,000 difference. CPU-only on already-saved outputs, roughly $5-25, no new GPU inference.\",\"compute_after\":\"If the gain is resolvable and S_inf sits well above the 50-member score, further compute should buy diversity (models, training seeds) rather than draws; if the CI includes zero, no member count on 7 dates can answer the root question and compute must buy dates. Either way, members past roughly 400 stop changing the answer.\",\"exact\":\"Per date, variable (10 m wind, 2 m temperature, 24 h precipitation), and lead: fair CRPS and Brier score for exceedance of the ERA5 99th climatological percentile at N in {50,100,200,400,800,1000}; fitted S_inf and alpha; 95% percentile-bootstrap CI (1,000 resamples over the 7 dates) of delta = score(1000) - score(50).\",\"expected\":\"alpha near 0.5-1 (textbook exchangeable-draw Monte Carlo, consistent with HENS-style convergence), S_inf within a few percent of the 1,000-member score, and a 7-date CI on delta wide enough that 'skill keeps rising past 50' is only weakly supported - the ladder mostly re-measures an asymptote already reached.\",\"fails_if\":\"The fitted decay is clearly slower than O(1/N) or the 500-to-1,000 step breaks the fit, meaning members are not exchangeable draws (correlated tail structure); then more members genuinely buy new information and the original ladder is the right design.\",\"closest_prior\":\"HENS Part 2 [s_hens] (7,424 SFNO members for tail sampling) and classical ensemble-size convergence results (Leutbecher 2019 on ensemble size; Richardson 2001 on ensemble-size effects in CRPS-type scores), which show scores approach an asymptote set by model error.\"},{\"index\":2,\"bottleneck\":\"GPU inference per member is the cost driver ($963 for 7,000 rollouts), yet if members are exchangeable draws, the ensemble at each gridpoint-lead is just samples from one smooth distribution; beyond the count needed to estimate that distribution, every extra rollout adds literally zero new information.\",\"assumption\":\"A 'member' must be produced by a 15-day autoregressive model rollout on a GPU - the unit of work is one forecast integration.\",\"reframe\":\"Change the unit of work: estimate the predictive distribution per gridpoint-lead from about 100 members (parametric tail fit - Gaussian body plus generalized Pareto tail - or quantile interpolation on sorted members), then draw arbitrarily many virtual members on CPU. If virtual-10,000 reproduces real-1,000 extreme scores, the member-count question is answered at any size without further GPU time, and 'members per forecast' stops being a compute axis at all.\",\"question\":\"Does a distribution fitted to 100 AIFS-ENS members, resampled to 10,000 virtual members, reproduce the real 1,000-member top-percentile Brier and fair-CRPS scores within the real run's own bootstrap noise?\",\"measure\":\"On the cheapest pilot stage (the $19.90 check-first run, 1-2 dates with at least 100 saved members): fit per-gridpoint-lead distributions, draw 10,000 virtual members, score extremes, and compare against nested real-member subsamples. Hours of CPU, roughly $2-15, runnable before any of the main $963 is committed.\",\"compute_after\":\"If the fit holds, infinite-member skill becomes a CPU calculation and the entire GPU budget redirects to more dates or more models; from then on, more compute changes the answer only through dates or diversity, never through member count.\",\"exact\":\"Per gridpoint-lead, exceedance probability of the ERA5 99th percentile; report the maximum absolute difference and bootstrap CI between virtual-10,000 and real-1,000 Brier and fair-CRPS scores, plus tail-fit error (Anderson-Darling statistic on the top 5% of members).\",\"expected\":\"The body fits well and 99th-percentile probabilities match within noise for wind and temperature; precipitation tails are heavier and need the Pareto component. Overall the fit reproduces the 50-to-1,000 curve, showing member counts beyond roughly 200 are a solved, GPU-free problem.\",\"fails_if\":\"Tail-fit error at the 99th percentile exceeds the 100-to-1,000 Monte Carlo gain - e.g., multimodal or strongly spatially correlated tail structure that a per-gridpoint fit destroys - in which case real rollouts remain the only honest sampler and the original plan stands.\",\"closest_prior\":\"HENS [s_hens] treats members as draws to be multiplied by GPU; the ensemble post-processing literature (EMOS, member-by-member statistical dressing, Scheuerer-Hamill-style resampling) already replaces extra members with fitted samplers at near-zero marginal cost.\"},{\"index\":3,\"bottleneck\":\"The root question's second clause - shared model error caps skill - cannot be isolated by adding more draws of the same distribution: 1,000 AIFS-ENS members share every bias with 50, so the planned spend can measure the asymptote but never what lies beyond it. Compute buys more of the same error structure.\",\"assumption\":\"The comparison that matters is N members of AIFS-ENS versus 50 members of AIFS-ENS, i.e., member count is the axis along which skill must be won or lost.\",\"reframe\":\"Change the objective and comparison: hold total members fixed and vary the number of distinct model distributions they are drawn from - 150 members as 150xAIFS-ENS versus a pool of 50 AIFS-ENS + 50 GraphCast-family + 50 SFNO/HENS-family. If the mixed pool at 150 beats even 1,000 AIFS-ENS members on extremes, shared error is proven to be the cap and the real compute lever is diversity, not count.\",\"question\":\"Does a 150-member pool drawn from three different ML model families beat 1,000 exchangeable AIFS-ENS members on top-percentile wind Brier skill for the same 7 dates?\",\"measure\":\"Download open-archive forecasts for the same 7 dates (ECMWF open data for AIFS-ENS; open GraphCast/Pangu/SFNO outputs, or re-run small open models on the existing GPUs), pool members, and re-score with the identical pipeline. Roughly $20-80 dominated by data movement and scoring, using 0-2 of the planned GPU-days if open archives cover the dates.\",\"compute_after\":\"If diversity wins, the scale-up path changes: the $3,980 full-scale spend buys 3 model families at roughly 330 members each across 30 dates instead of 1,000 members of one model - more compute then buys genuinely new information per dollar rather than re-sampling one distribution.\",\"exact\":\"Brier skill score and fair CRPS for 99th-percentile exceedance (wind, temperature, rain versus ERA5), pooled over leads of 3-10 days, for AIFS-ENS-150, AIFS-ENS-1000, and MIX-150 (50 per model family); report pairwise deltas with date-bootstrap CIs.\",\"expected\":\"MIX-150 clearly beats AIFS-ENS-150 and matches or beats AIFS-ENS-1000 on wind and temperature extremes, because member error decorrelates across model families - demonstrating that the cap is shared error and that roughly 950 of the planned 1,000 members buy almost nothing.\",\"fails_if\":\"AIFS-ENS-1000 beats MIX-150 on all three variables, meaning one well-trained afCRPS distribution dominates and cross-model diversity adds noise rather than skill; then member count (or single-model quality) really is the lever and the original design is right.\",\"closest_prior\":\"HENS [s_hens] shows huge single-model ensembles sample 4-sigma tails but cannot remove shared bias; multi-model and grand-ensemble results in NWP, and ML multi-model comparisons around AIFS/GraphCast/Pangu, consistently show diversity beating raw size at fixed cost.\"}]
